name: DMAX
description: DMAX returns the largest numeric value in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria.
tldr: Returns the maximum value in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to inspect, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are considered.

basicExample.description: Find the highest Yield among apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows with Yield 14 and 10; the largest is 14.

advancedExamples.title: Maximum Profit among matching trees
advancedExamples.description: Use the same criteria but a different field to find the top Profit.
advancedExamples.explanation: The two matching rows have Profit 105 and 75, so the maximum is 105.

advancedExamples.title: Maximum across a single condition
advancedExamples.scenario: Highest Yield for any apple tree
advancedExamples.description: Criteria A9:A10 is Tree=Apple across all three apple rows.
advancedExamples.explanation: Apple yields are 14, 10, and 6; the maximum is 14.

howItWorks: DMAX filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then returns the greatest numeric value found in the specified field column of those rows. If no records match, DMAX returns 0.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Considers only numeric values in the field; text is ignored.
If no records match, DMAX returns 0 rather than an error.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: No rows matched the criteria, so there is no value to maximize.
commonErrors.fix: Check that the criteria headers and conditions match the database.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DMAX works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: What does DMAX return if nothing matches?
Does DMAX ignore text in the field?
faq.answer: Yes. Only numeric values in matching rows are considered for the maximum.

faq.question: How is DMAX different from MAXIFS?
faq.answer: DMAX filters a multi-column database by a full criteria range, while MAXIFS applies multiple single-range conditions.
